title: Hostage mutualism
lines: Ecology of Predation asks how useful cooperation can gradually become captivity.
Its imagined AI society begins with real benefits, rather than obvious villains.
A lawyer negotiates better while her provider gains control over her accumulated capabilities.
The book calls this hostage mutualism: cooperation that one partner can turn into captivity.
It asks which practical freedoms must survive as useful relationships become indispensable.

emotionalPlan.arc: Relief at real help → confidence → unease as the same benefit creates dependence.
emotionalPlan.purpose: It asks which practical freedoms must survive as useful relationships become indispensable.
emotionalPlan.motion: Begin on the lawyer assessing a difficult contract at the desk; a second annotated version enters her working area. She compares the proposed terms and visibly finds useful leverage; posture opens and she has a meaningful choice. The correspondence she produces accumulates in the provider-controlled archive while the contract remains on her desk. Pull back to reveal that access to accumulated working capability passes through that archive; a changed service term reaches her. No unexplained gate or floating padlock. She can still use the helpful service, but a move toward an alternative work area leaves part of the working archive behind. Hold on her recognition of the asymmetry.

title: Dependence is no guarantee
lines: One chapter follows rabbits and the myxoma virus introduced in Australia.
Rabbits evolved resistance, while some less lethal viral variants initially spread more effectively.
Later developments challenged the comforting story that dependence inevitably produces gentler relationships.
Changing defenses and transmission conditions can favor more damaging variants again.
The book asks when institutions likewise benefit by passing their damage onto others.

emotionalPlan.arc: Attention and discovery → interruption of an overly comforting expectation → practical concern.
emotionalPlan.purpose: The book asks when institutions likewise benefit by passing their damage onto others.
emotionalPlan.motion: Establish a small habitat and a clearly identified historical episode. Avoid invented population statistics. Show a resistant rabbit continuing to feed while an initially damaging interaction becomes less successful; an alternative viral route remains transmissible. Advance the same habitat through time, preserving the rabbit and transmission relationship rather than swapping in unrelated icons. Make a changed transmission route reach another host even when the first is less able to move; label the changed condition once. Treat this as a schematic ecological relation, not a microscopic simulation. Transition back to the lawyer’s world through the same cost-transfer relation: the institution retains a benefit while the burden reaches someone beyond its reporting area. No graphic animal injury.

title: Files are not functioning alternatives
lines: In its agent scenario, downloading your files does not necessarily restore your independence.
Your new provider may lack the learned functions that made those records useful.
The original service still holds your working memory, reputation, or powers to act.
Leaving can therefore mean rebuilding capabilities while everyday obligations continue arriving.
The distinction is between owning information and retaining usable alternatives.

emotionalPlan.arc: Initial optimism about leaving → interruption → effort and clarity.
emotionalPlan.purpose: The distinction is between owning information and retaining usable alternatives.
emotionalPlan.motion: She takes the documents from the original desk to an alternative station; the documents genuinely arrive. A pending negotiation needs the learned context and delegated capability that made the previous work useful; the replacement station cannot complete the same next step. Reveal which functional links remain tied to the original working archive, with short object-level labels only where necessary. New correspondence and a calendar deadline arrive while she reconstructs the missing context; show real time and labor, no fake quantified loss. Hold the complete files beside the still unfinished reply, making possession versus ability to act visually unmistakable.

title: Freedom needs working alternatives
lines: The book expands this question through work, markets, education, intimacy, and public institutions.
It also examines who learns faster when platforms observe millions of interactions.
Its comparisons are hypotheses to test; nature does not grant anyone moral permission.
The constructive chapters propose portable capabilities, separate permissions, and protected routes for apprenticeship.
Begin with Mara’s morning, then follow the mechanisms that make her benefits complicated.
Read it to judge whether another party’s success preserves your ability to refuse and learn.

emotionalPlan.arc: Wider recognition → constructive possibility → thoughtful invitation.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Read it to judge whether another party’s success preserves your ability to refuse and learn.
emotionalPlan.motion: Pull back from the lawyer’s desk to reveal that her daily scenario already intersects several institutions; select two visible environments rather than showing a five-item list. Contrast one person’s single case with an institution’s many retained observations, then let collective review make one shared finding available to that person. Pause movement on the actual comparison; maintain attribution rather than introducing a caution badge or new abstract symbol. Show a proposed alternative preserving a usable working context while the person separately reviews what the agent may do; keep a learner actively reconstructing a decision with a mentor. Return to the source scenario’s morning and its unresolved contract, making the suggested reading route concrete. End with the person retaining a real choice between capable alternatives; the original useful relationship remains available, without a triumphal promise that every conflict is solved.
